item.title: Caterpillar rides AI boom but warns of tariff hit ahead
item.description: Caterpillar’s quarterly results were boosted by AI-driven demand for power systems, but the company warned tariffs could cost more than $2 billion.

item.title: Senators seek certainty for approved infrastructure projects
item.description: Republicans and Democrats say fully permitted U.S. infrastructure projects should not be stalled or canceled due to shifting political priorities.

item.title: Trump administration steps back from critical minerals price floors
item.description: The Trump administration is backing away from guaranteeing price floors for U.S. critical minerals projects, citing funding limits and legal risks.

item.title: Trump EPA delays repeal of climate rule over legal concerns
item.description: Trump administration officials have delayed repealing the EPA’s climate endangerment finding amid concerns the proposal may not survive court challenges.

item.title: U.S. trade deficit posts biggest jump in nearly 34 years
item.description: The U.S. trade deficit surged nearly 95% in November as imports jumped on strong demand for capital goods tied to AI investment, government data shows.

item.title: On the Market: Retail and institutional properties
item.description: This week’s On the Market features a St. Paul institutional building, a high-occupancy Minneapolis retail center, and a Baxter retail redevelopment opportunity.

item.title: Wisconsin contractors adopt workplace harassment program
item.description: Wisconsin construction contractors are adopting bystander training to prevent workplace harassment, bullying and violence on job sites statewide.

item.title: St. Cloud backs sales tax for YMCA water park project
item.description: St. Cloud leaders approved steps toward a 0.25% sales tax to help fund a YMCA water park, pending state approval and a 2026 referendum.

item.title: Costs stymie many first-time homebuyers, Realtors report
item.description: Minnesota home sales under $300,000 fell 6% in 2025 while $1 million-plus sales jumped 22%, highlighting affordability challenges for first-time buyers.

item.title: Metro housing starts up, but headwinds remain
item.description: Twin Cities housing starts rose 22% in January as permits climbed, but experts warn multifamily construction still faces financing and labor challenges.
